title: Why Brown Butter Mashed Potatoes Beat $20 Steakhouse Sides
description: Make ultra-silky brown butter mashed potatoes at home in just 20 minutes. Skip pricey steakhouse sides and save cash with this easy weeknight recipe.
story: After a grueling eight-hour workday staring at spreadsheets in my cramped apartment, the last thing I wanted was a complicated dinner. I was craving that ultra-rich, nutty side dish from the local bistro that easily costs $12 a plate, but my grocery budget was screaming at me to use what was already in the fridge. I raided my pantry, grabbed a bag of russets from Aldi, and decided to channel my inner French chef with a quick stick of butter. Let me tell you, browning that butter in my trusty skillet completely transformed basic spuds into something wildly luxurious for less than four bucks total. No fancy equipment needed, just pure comfort food magic that saved my weeknight.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
4 tablespoons unsalted butter (Kerrygold works best for richness)
1/3 cup whole milk or heavy cream, warmed
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more for the boiling water
2 tablespoons fresh chives, finely chopped for garnish
instructions: Step 1: Place your cubed potatoes in a medium pot, cover with cold salted water, and bring to a boil. Cook for about 12 minutes until fork-tender, then drain well.

Step 2: While the potatoes boil, melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Swirl the pan occasionally until the butter foams, turns golden brown, and smells nutty—about 3 to 4 minutes. (Watch it closely, the first time I tested this I burnt the garlic because I cranked the heat too high!)
Step 3: Toss the smashed garlic cloves into the warm brown butter for the last 30 seconds of melting to infuse that cozy, savory flavor, then discard the cloves.
Step 4: Mash the drained potatoes with warm milk, pour in the hot brown butter, and whip vigorously with a hand masher or wooden spoon until smooth and silky.
proHack: Always use warm milk when adding it to your potatoes. Cold milk lowers the temperature of the spuds too fast and makes the starches gummy instead of velvety and smooth.
storage: Store leftover mashed potatoes in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop over low heat with a splash of milk or chicken broth to bring back that creamy texture.

faqs.question: Can I substitute milk if I don't have heavy cream?
faqs.answer: Totally! Regular whole milk, half-and-half, or even a splash of unsweetened almond milk mixed with a little extra butter works great in a pinch.

faqs.question: How do I prevent my potatoes from turning gluey?
faqs.answer: Avoid using a food processor or electric mixer, which breaks down the starch too fast. Stick to a hand potato masher or a sturdy wooden spoon for the best fluffy texture.
